# app-tokens revoke

Command: `boundary app-tokens revoke`

The `app-tokens revoke` command revokes an app token given its ID. Revoking an app
token permanently deactivates it. You can no longer use a revoked app token to
authorize actions in Boundary.

## Example

The following example revokes an app token with the ID, `appt_1234567890`.

```shell-session
$ boundary app-tokens revoke -id appt_1234567890
```

## Usage

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```shell-session
$ boundary app-tokens revoke [options] [args]
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

### Command options

- `-id` `(string: "")` - The ID of the app token to revoke.
